Algar do Carvão.note: Natural 45 m entrance pit (the algar itself): center of the large radial-hachure ring in the SIGCAVA drawing, with the visitor spiral staircases vectorized inside it.
Artificial access tunnel portal (1963 visitor tunnel): NW end of the straight double line that runs from the surface into the pit rim.

Gruta do Natal.note: Main managed entrance: radial-tick shaft circle connected by two ladder/stair bands to the drawn visitor building rectangle (SW corner of cave). The show cave has two managed entrances.
Small man-made quadrilateral drawn on the tube 45 m N of the main stairs - best candidate for the second managed (exit) stairway. Web sources only confirm 'two staircases' without a map.
Tiny square structure at the very NE tip of the long NE gallery; possible third opening, unverified.

Gruta das Agulhas.note: Single land entrance at the inland (N) tip of the tube; small closed tip with rock blob drawn. GBIF entrance fix is 19 m NE of the nearest wall vertex - good georeferencing agreement.
Sea opening at Ponta dos Coelhos: the tube walls end in a gap between two coastal-cliff hachure lines drawn at the S end. Enter only at low tide with a calm sea.

Gruta dos Balcões.note: Large collapse doline (30x16 m radial-hachure oval) in the NW sector - the main entrance collapse. GBIF fix lies 185 m WNW of the drawing (georef disagreement); its snap vertex is only 28 m from this doline, supporting it as the entrance.
Second, smaller radial-hachure ring (8 m) with breakdown field, 25 m NE of the main doline.
6 m radial-hachure ring at the S tip of the network. Cave is 'fractured by ceiling collapses' - multiple skylights likely; only rings actually drawn are listed.

Gruta da Branca Opala.note: Upstream ('a montante') skylight entrance: 8.5 m radial-hachure ring at the S/SE end. Borges et al. 1994: three entrances, the first upstream is a skylight, the tube collects torrential water there.
GBIF entrance fix snapped 70 m to the N (downstream) end of the drawing; plausibly one of the two 'recent collapse' entrances of the 1994 text. Exact position on drawing unknown.

Gruta do Chocolate.note: 40x40 cm hole entered 'por uma galeria secundária' (Montanheiros): tiny oval drawn inside the forked SW branch tip. GBIF fix is 21 m S of this tip - corroborates the southern end.

Gruta do Caldeira.note: Small oval with leader line drawn at the S fork junction; same mark appears in Borges et al. 1994 Fig 5, whose station numbering starts here. 1986 description: small hole noticed by air condensation; both tube ends terminate in impassable collapses. No GBIF fix.

Gruta da Madre de Deus.note: Walk-in entrance chamber ('sala de grande amplitude', station 0 of Borges et al. 1994 Fig 10): 10.5 m radial-hachure circle at the SE extremity, with surface-rock 'toes' drawn beyond it. GBIF fix sits 40 m W of mid-tube, matching neither end (ambiguous).

Second entrance: 13.5 m vertical algar at station 24 (1994 text, Fig 10 '?' tip) = extreme NW tip of the breakdown-filled chamber. Note: the CSV attributes the 13.5 m pit to Mercês II, but the 1994 page-21 text referencing Fig 10 belongs to Madre de Deus.

Gruta da Malha.note: GBIF entrance fix snapped 27 m E to the west wall of the tube (local mid-south sector). No entrance mark identifiable in the drawing at this spot.
Largest collapse feature in the drawing: 18x15 m radial-hachure rim spanning the tube ~55 m N of the GBIF snap - candidate entrance collapse.

Gruta do Coelho.note: Main entrance ('toca de coelho' rabbit-hole, Borges et al. 1994): E mark pair flanking the rung-hatched narrow passage at section a-a of Fig 7; the rung feature is unambiguously identifiable in the vector. GBIF fix is 148 m NW of the drawing (large georef disagreement) - all placements are in drawing space.
Second E (entrada) mark of Fig 7 at the central mud-zone gallery edge (gallery from section e-e 'passa por duas entradas').
Third E mark of Fig 7, at the junction with the dashed (unsurveyed) loop, next to a stipple patch; position transferred by similarity fit with ~5 m residuals.

Gruta dos Principiantes.note: Entrance at a roof collapse ('abatimento onde está a respectiva entrada' - Freguesia de Biscoitos page): upper hachured collapse rim crossing the tube in the southern third. GBIF fix is 26 m W - good agreement. Tube continues upslope (S) beyond, blocked with soil (dashed S tip).

Furna de Santa Maria.note: GBIF fix (49 m NW) snaps exactly onto the stippled debris-cone feature drawn against the N wall of the main chamber - classic under-opening breakdown cone; best entrance estimate. Caveat: drawing extent (~20x55 m) is far smaller than the stated 320 m length - SIGCAVA georeferencing/scale of this drawing is suspect.
NE head of the drawn double line (path/water channel with two small square structures - Cabrito water-supply area) descending into the cave; possible man-made access.

Galeria da Queimada.note: Only candidate mark in the drawing: hachured half-circle bite in the E wall of the W gallery plus a small circle drawn beside it (and water-line dashes inside). No GBIF fix and no textual entrance description found.

N tip: walls end open (drawing cut) - possible entrance/continuation. Matches the N extremity given in the field notes (38.75253, -27.2679 approx.). S extremity (38.750045,-27.266568) is drawn closed.

_meta.frame: All points lie in SIGCAVA survey-drawing space (EPSG:4326) so they overlay correctly on the gfi_ln polylines; absolute accuracy is limited by each drawing's georeferencing.
sources: Borges, Pereira & Silva 1994 'Grutas e Algares dos Açores I - Seis novas topografias' (Figs 5, 7, 10 + text)
